# Model reference

This is the reference of the document model: every node kind, enumeration, target kind and category declared with the model's declaration forms, by area. Field names are their JSON names. A required field is present in every node of its kind. Examples are written as S-expressions.

## Structure

### Node kind `:document`

The whole standard: the root of the model, built from every chapter
job.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | The revision of the draft, the text of \rev in setup-version.tex. |
| `front-matter` | list of node of kind or category `:chapter` | no | The unnumbered chapters of chap-0.tex (\beginSimpleChapter), in order; absent when the model is built from part of the jobs. |
| `chapters` | list of node of kind or category `:chapter` | yes | The numbered chapters (\beginchapter), 1 to 26, then the appendix A, in that order. |

### Node kind `:chapter`

A chapter: a numbered one begun by \beginchapter, or an unnumbered
one of the front matter begun by \beginSimpleChapter or
\beginSimpleChapterLeft.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The chapter's id: the reference name of \beginchapter (its third argument, e.g. ChapOne), or a simple chapter's title. |
| `number` | string | no | The chapter's number as \beginchapter's first argument gives it ("1" … "26", "A"); absent for a simple chapter. |
| `title` | inline list | yes | The chapter's title, \beginchapter's second argument or the simple chapter's one. |
| `children` | list of node of kind or category `:section`, `:dictionary-entry`, `:block` | no | What the chapter holds, in order: the blocks before its first section, then its sections. |

### Node kind `:section`

A section of any level: \beginSection or \includeDictionary (level
1), \beginSubsection (2), \beginsubsubsection (3),
\beginsubsubsubsection (4) or \beginsubsubsubsubsection (5).  It runs
to the next section of its level or above, or the chapter's end.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The label of the \DefineSection that names the section, or <parent-id>/<n> for a section that none names (its n-th among its parent's sections). |
| `number` | string | yes | The section's number, its chapter's and the count of each level joined by dots ("14.1.2"), as the :write of its \DefineSection confirms. |
| `level` | integer | yes | The level, 1 for a section of the chapter, 2 for a subsection, and so on to 5. |
| `dictionary` | boolean | no | True for a dictionary section, begun by \includeDictionary: its children are dictionary entries. |
| `title` | inline list | yes | The section's title, the argument of the macro that began it. |
| `children` | list of node of kind or category `:section`, `:dictionary-entry`, `:glossary-group`, `:block` | no | What the section holds, in order: blocks, dictionary entries, glossary groups and its subsections. |

### Target kind `:chapter`

A chapter, by its id: the target of a \secref whose label a
\DefineChapter defines.

A reference of this kind points to a node of kind `:chapter`.

### Target kind `:section`

A section of any level, by its id: the target of a \secref whose
label a \DefineSection defines.

A reference of this kind points to a node of kind `:section`.

## Entries

### Node kind `:dictionary-entry`

A dictionary entry, from \begincom to \endcom: the description of
one or more defined names of one kind.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The entry's id: its first name, or <name>/<entry-kind> when two entries share a first name (docs/exports.md, "Ids"). |
| `names` | list of string | yes | The names the entry describes, the comma-separated list of \begincom's first argument, in order. |
| `entry-kind` | enumeration `entry-kind` | yes | What the names are, from the entry's \ftype. |
| `parts` | list of node of kind or category `:part` | no | The entry's parts, one per \label, in order. |

### Node kind `:part`

A part of a dictionary entry: a \label heading (Syntax, Arguments and
Values, Description, …) and what follows it up to the next \label or
the entry's end.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes | The heading, the text of the \label before its colon. |
| `none` | boolean | no | True when the part says only "None." (\None after the \label). |
| `content` | list of node of kind or category `:block` | no | The part's blocks; absent when NONE is true. |

### Node kind `:operator-signature`

The syntax of an operator as a Syntax part sets it: \Defun,
\Defmac, \Defspec, \Defgen and their WithValues, WithValuesNewline
and NoReturn variants, \Defmeth, \DefunMultiWithValues, and the
reader half of \DefunMultiAccessorWithValues.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operator` | enumeration `operator` | yes | The kind of operator, by the macro. |
| `names` | list of string | yes | The operator's name, or the names of the \entry lines of a -Multi form, which share the lambda list and values. |
| `lambda-list` | inline list | no | The lambda list as written, with its parameters and lambda list keywords; absent when empty. |
| `values` | inline list | no | The values as written after the arrow; absent for a form without values (\Defun, \Defmeth) and when NO-RETURN is true. |
| `no-return` | boolean | no | True for a NoReturn form: the operator never returns normally. |

### Node kind `:setf-signature`

The syntax of a setf form: \Defsetf, \DefsetfMulti, and the setf
half of \DefunMultiAccessorWithValues.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | list of string | yes | The accessor's name, or the names of the \entry lines of a -Multi form. |
| `lambda-list` | inline list | no | The accessor's lambda list as written; absent when empty. |
| `new-value` | inline list | yes | The new value as written. |

### Node kind `:variable-signature`

The syntax of a variable or a constant: \Defvar, \Defvarnoast,
\Defcon.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The variable's name, with its asterisks when the source sets them. |
| `constant` | boolean | no | True for a constant variable (\Defcon). |

### Node kind `:type-signature`

The syntax of a compound type specifier: \Deftype.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The type specifier's symbol. |
| `syntax` | inline list | no | The lines of the compound form after the name, with their BNF notation; absent when there are none. |

### Enumeration `entry-kind`

What a dictionary entry defines: the text of its \ftype, in
kebab-case.  A variant spelling of one of these in the sources is fixed
by a patch, not by a value of its own.

- `:function` - An ordinary function, called with evaluated arguments
(\ftype{Function}).
- `:system-class` - A class the implementation may define as a built-in
class rather than a standard class (\ftype{System Class}).
- `:macro` - A global macro, expanded before evaluation (\ftype{Macro}).
- `:condition-type` - A type of condition, signalled to the handlers
(\ftype{Condition Type}).
- `:variable` - A dynamic variable whose value may change
(\ftype{Variable}).
- `:type` - A type that is not a class (\ftype{Type}).
- `:accessor` - A function that reads a place and, through setf, writes
it (\ftype{Accessor}).
- `:standard-generic-function` - A generic function of the standard, whose methods users may addn(\ftype{Standard Generic Function}).
- `:special-operator` - An operator with its own evaluation rule, not a
macro or function (\ftype{Special Operator}).
- `:type-specifier` - A symbol that is only a compound type specifier,
naming no type alone (\ftype{Type Specifier}).
- `:constant-variable` - A variable whose value never changes
(\ftype{Constant Variable}).
- `:declaration` - The identifier of a declaration, used in declare and
proclaim (\ftype{Declaration}).
- `:restart` - The name of a restart the standard establishes or invokes
(\ftype{Restart}).
- `:local-macro` - A macro defined only within another form (\ftype{Local Macro}).
- `:class` - A standard class, defined as by defclass (\ftype{Class}).
- `:symbol` - A symbol described for its own sake, neither operator,
variable nor type (\ftype{Symbol}).
- `:local-function` - A function defined only within another form (\ftype{Local Function}).

### Enumeration `operator`

The kind of operator a signature describes, by the macro that sets it.

- `:function` - A function: \Defun and its variants, \DefunMultiWithValues.
- `:macro` - A macro: \Defmac and its variants.
- `:special-operator` - A special operator: \Defspec and its variants.
- `:generic-function` - A generic function: \Defgen and its variants.
- `:method` - A method of a generic function: \Defmeth.

### Target kind `:entry`

A dictionary entry, by its id: the target of \clref and its
wrappers (\funref, \macref, …).

A reference of this kind points to a node of kind `:dictionary-entry`.

## Blocks

### Node kind `:paragraph`

A paragraph: the text TeX set from the start of horizontal mode to
\par.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The paragraph's text and inlines, in order. |

### Node kind `:code-block`

Code, from \code to \endcode, each line as it is written.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lines` | list of node of kind or category `:code-line` | yes | The lines, in order, blank ones included. |

### Node kind `:code-line`

A line of a code block.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | no | The line's text, its spaces kept, and its inlines (terms, example notation); absent for a blank line. |

### Node kind `:item-list`

A list, from \beginlist to \endlist, or the items of a level below
\item (\itemitem, \itemitemitem) that follow one another.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of node of kind or category `:item` | yes | The list's items, in order. |

### Node kind `:item`

An item of a list: \item, \itemitem or \itemitemitem and what
follows it up to the next item of its level or above, or the list's
end.  Items of a lower level after it form an item list in its content.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | inline list | no | The item's label, the macro's argument (a bullet, a number, a term); absent when empty. |
| `content` | list of node of kind or category `:block` | no | The item's blocks. |

### Node kind `:editor-note`

An editor's note, \editornote: a remark of the editors, not part of
the standard, kept whatever the options say.

Categories: `:block`, `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The note's text. |
| `hidden` | boolean | no | True when the options (\editornotesfalse) hide the note from the typeset document. |

### Node kind `:reviewer-note`

A reviewer's note, \reviewer: a remark of a reviewer, not part of
the standard, kept whatever the options say.

Categories: `:block`, `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The note's text. |
| `hidden` | boolean | no | True when the options (\editornotesfalse) hide the note from the typeset document. |

### Category `:block`

What stands between paragraphs in a section, a part or an item:
paragraphs, code, lists, tables, figures, signatures, BNF rules,
displayed math, notes and the anchors that fall between blocks.

Kinds: `:operator-signature`, `:setf-signature`, `:variable-signature`, `:type-signature`, `:paragraph`, `:code-block`, `:item-list`, `:editor-note`, `:reviewer-note`, `:table`, `:figure`, `:index-entry`, `:issue-start`, `:issue-end`, `:bnf-rule`, `:math`.

## Tables

### Node kind `:table`

A table: an alignment (\halign, as \tabletwo, \tablefigtwo …,
\displaytwo … and \showtwo … set it) read as rows of cells.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` | list of node of kind or category `:row` | yes | The table's rows, in order. |

### Node kind `:row`

A row of a table.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `header` | boolean | no | True for a row of column headings (the heading arguments of \tablefigtwo and its relatives). |
| `cells` | list of node of kind or category `:cell` | yes | The row's cells, in order. |

### Node kind `:cell`

A cell of a row.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | no | The cell's text and inlines; absent for an empty cell. |
| `columns` | integer | no | The number of columns the cell spans when \span joined more than one; absent for one. |

### Node kind `:figure`

A figure: a numbered display with a caption (\endfig, \tablefigtwo
and its relatives).

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The label of the \DefineFigure that names the figure, or <chapter-id>/fig-<n> for a figure that none names. |
| `number` | string | yes | The figure's number, its chapter's and its own joined by a hyphen ("14-1"), from the caption, checked against the :write of its \DefineFigure when there is one. |
| `caption` | inline list | no | The caption's text after the number; absent when the figure has none. |
| `content` | list of node of kind or category `:block` | yes | What the figure shows: a table, or other blocks. |

### Target kind `:figure`

A figure, by its id: the target of \figref and \thenextfigure.

A reference of this kind points to a node of kind `:figure`.

## Inlines

### Node kind `:term-ref`

A use of a glossary term: \term, or \newterm and \newtermidx where
the text defines the term.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The term as written, inflected ("dotted lists"). |
| `defining` | boolean | no | True for \newterm and \newtermidx: the use defines the term. |
| `sense` | integer | no | The glossary sense meant, from the \meaning that follows; absent when none does. |
| `target` | reference (target `:glossary`) | no | The glossary entry of the term; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:term-ref :text "dotted lists" :target (:glossary "dotted list"))
```

### Node kind `:operator-ref`

A reference to a defined name: \clref and its wrappers.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The name as the reference sets it. |
| `via` | enumeration `reference-kind` | yes | The macro the reference was written with. |
| `target` | reference (target `:entry`) | no | The dictionary entry of the name; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:operator-ref :text "endp" :via :function :target (:entry "endp"))
```

### Node kind `:section-ref`

A reference to a section or a chapter: \secref.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | yes | The label referred to, as written after \secref. |
| `target` | reference (target `:section`, `:chapter`) | no | The section or chapter of the label; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:section-ref :label "OrdinaryLambdaLists" :target
 (:section "OrdinaryLambdaLists"))
```

### Node kind `:figure-ref`

A reference to a figure: \figref.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | yes | The label referred to, as written after \figref. |
| `target` | reference (target `:figure`) | no | The figure of the label; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:figure-ref :label "FigConses" :target (:figure "14-1"))
```

### Node kind `:this-section`

The words `this section': \thissection, \Thissection, a reference to
the section they are in.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | reference (target `:section`) | no | The section the words are in; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:this-section :target (:section "Conses"))
```

### Node kind `:next-figure`

The words `Figure N-M' for the figure that follows: \thenextfigure,
\Thenextfigure.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | reference (target `:figure`) | no | The next figure; absent while unresolved. |

Example:

```lisp
(:next-figure :target (:figure "14-1"))
```

### Node kind `:param`

A parameter of the operator described: \param.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The parameter's name. |

Example:

A metavariable, in double angle brackets: \metavar, \metaparam.

### Node kind `:lambda-list-keyword`

A lambda list keyword in a lambda list: \opt, \rest, \key and their

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|


### Node kind `:citation`

The title of a work the standard cites: \CLtL, \CLtLTwo and the

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The title as set. |

### Node kind `:index-entry`

An entry of the index: an anchor where the text indexes a name or a
phrase, \idxref and its relatives.

Categories: `:inline`, `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index-kind` | enumeration `index-kind` | yes | What is indexed. |
| `text` | string | yes | The indexed text, as written. |

Example:

```lisp

```

### Node kind `:issue-start`

Where the text an X3J13 issue brought begins: \issue.  Issues are
ranges that may cross blocks and sections, so they are anchors.

Categories: `:inline`, `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The issue's name, e.g. "DOTTED-LIST-ARGUMENTS:CLARIFY". |

Example:

```lisp
(:issue-start :name "DOTTED-LIST-ARGUMENTS:CLARIFY")
```

### Node kind `:issue-end`

Where the text an X3J13 issue brought ends: \endissue, the one end
of the issue-start before it with its name.

Categories: `:inline`, `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The issue's name. |

Example:

```lisp
(:issue-end :name "DOTTED-LIST-ARGUMENTS:CLARIFY")
```

### Enumeration `reference-kind`

The macro a reference to a defined name was written with, which says
what kind of name it means.

- `:any` - \clref: a defined name of any kind.
- `:function` - \funref: a function.
- `:macro` - \macref: a macro.
- `:special-operator` - \specref: a special operator.
- `:type` - \typeref: a type or a class.
- `:variable` - \varref: a variable.
- `:constant` - \conref: a constant variable.
- `:declaration` - \declref: a declaration identifier.
- `:package` - \packref: a package.
- `:keyword` - \kwd, \kwdref: a keyword, written with its colon.
- `:loop-keyword` - \loopref: a loop keyword.
- `:lambda-list-keyword` - \keyref: a lambda list keyword, written with its
ampersand.
- `:typewriter` - \ttref: a name set in the typewriter font.
- `:misc` - \misc, \miscref: a symbol of no other kind (t, nil, a
restart).

### Enumeration `index-kind`

What an index entry indexes, by its macro.

- `:ref` - \idxref: a defined name.
- `:keyref` - \idxkeyref: a lambda list keyword, without its ampersand.
- `:code` - \idxcode: code.
- `:keyword` - \idxkwd: a keyword.
- `:text` - \idxtext: a phrase.
- `:term` - \idxterm: a glossary term.
- `:example` - \idxexample: an example.
- `:package` - \idxpackref: a package.

### Category `:inline`

What stands in running text beside strings: references, parameters,
code, emphasis, example notation, math, anchors.

Kinds: `:editor-note`, `:reviewer-note`, `:term-ref`, `:operator-ref`, `:section-ref`, `:figure-ref`, `:this-section`, `:next-figure`, `:param`, `:metavariable`, `:format-directive`, `:lambda-list-keyword`, `:code`, `:emphasis`, `:strong`, `:evaluates-to`, `:may-evaluate-to`, `:does-not-evaluate-to`, `:equivalent`, `:output`, `:input`, `:citation`, `:index-entry`, `:issue-start`, `:issue-end`, `:bnf-break`, `:bnf-optional`, `:bnf-zero-or-more`, `:bnf-one-or-more`, `:bnf-repeat-previous`, `:bnf-group`, `:bnf-parenthesized`, `:bnf-bracketed`, `:bnf-interleave`, `:bnf-required`, `:bnf-indirection`, `:bnf-caret`, `:angle-name`, `:math`.

## Glossary

### Node kind `:glossary-group`

The glossary entries under one letter heading, from \firstindextab
or \indextab to the next.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `letter` | string | yes | The heading's letter, or the heading for the entries that do not begin with a letter. |
| `entries` | list of node of kind or category `:glossary-entry` | no | The group's entries, in order. |

### Node kind `:glossary-entry`

A glossary entry, from \gentry to the next \gentry, \indextab or
the glossary's end.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The entry's id: its term. |
| `term` | string | yes | The term defined, \gentry's argument. |
| `pronunciation` | inline list | no | How the term is pronounced, \pronounced's argument, with its stress marks; absent when not given. |
| `parts-of-speech` | list of enumeration `part-of-speech` | no | The parts of speech given after the term, before the senses, in order. |
| `usages` | list of enumeration `usage` | no | The usages given after the term, before the senses, that hold for every sense. |
| `senses` | list of node of kind or category `:glossary-sense` | yes | The senses, in order; one, without a number, when the entry is not numbered. |

### Node kind `:glossary-sense`

A sense of a glossary term: a numbered definition (`1.', `2.', …), or
the entry's one definition.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `number` | integer | no | The sense's number; absent when the entry has one sense. |
| `parts-of-speech` | list of enumeration `part-of-speech` | no | The parts of speech given for this sense alone. |
| `usages` | list of enumeration `usage` | no | The usages given for this sense alone. |
| `content` | inline list | yes | The definition's text, its \term references and its `See' pointers. |
| `examples` | list of node of kind or category `:glossary-example` | no | The sense's examples, \gexample, in order. |

### Node kind `:glossary-example`

An example of a glossary sense, set in quotes: \gexample.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The example's text. |

### Enumeration `part-of-speech`

The part of speech of a glossary term, by its macro.

- `:noun` - \Noun, `n.'.
- `:verb` - \Verb, `v.'.
- `:transitive-verb` - \TransitiveVerb, `v.t.'.
- `:adjective` - \Adjective, `adj.'.
- `:adverb` - \Adverb, `adv.'.

### Enumeration `usage`

Where a glossary sense comes from or is used, by its macro.

- `:ansi` - \ANSI: a sense the standard itself fixes.
- `:ieee` - \IEEE: the sense of the IEEE standards.
- `:iso` - \ISO: the sense of the ISO standards.
- `:traditional` - \Traditional: a traditional sense, kept for
compatibility with earlier usage.
- `:mathematics` - \Mathematics: the sense of mathematics.
- `:idiomatic` - \Idiomatic: an idiomatic sense.
- `:computers` - \Computers: the sense of computing in general.

### Target kind `:glossary`

A glossary entry, by its id: the target of \term and \newterm.

A reference of this kind points to a node of kind `:glossary-entry`.

## BNF

### Node kind `:bnf-rule`

A BNF rule: \auxbnf, a non-terminal and its definition.

Categories: `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The non-terminal defined. |
| `definition` | inline list | yes | The right side, with its notation and line breaks; the name and the glyphs the notation macros typeset (brackets, parentheses, stars) are not repeated in it. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-rule :name "wholevar" :definition
 ((:bnf-bracketed :content ("&whole var"))))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-break`

A line break within the right side of a BNF rule: \CR.

Categories: `:inline`.

_No fields._

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-break)
```

### Node kind `:bnf-optional`

What may appear once or not at all, in brackets: \brac, or \lbrac
… \rbrac split over lines.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The optional part. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-optional :content ("supplied-p-parameter"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-zero-or-more`

What may appear any number of times, starred: \star.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | What repeats. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-zero-or-more :content ((:bnf-group :content ("var"))))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-one-or-more`

What appears one or more times, with a plus: \plus.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | What repeats. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-one-or-more :content ("var"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-repeat-previous`

A plus alone: what precedes appears one or more times (\prevplus,
after a group split over lines).

Categories: `:inline`.

_No fields._

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-repeat-previous)
```

### Node kind `:bnf-group`

A group, usually of alternatives, in braces: \curly, or \lcurly …
\rcurly split over lines.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The group's content. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-group :content ("var"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-parenthesized`

Its content in literal parentheses: \paren, or \lparen … \rparen.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | What the parentheses hold. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-parenthesized :content ("keyword-name var"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-bracketed`

Its content in literal brackets, in the code font: \ttbrac, or
\lttbrac … \rttbrac.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | What the brackets hold. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-bracketed :content ("&rest var"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-interleave`

Alternatives in any order, each at most once: \interleave, or
\begininterleave … \endinterleave.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | The alternatives. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-interleave :content
 ((:bnf-required :content ("A")) " " (:bnf-required :content ("B"))
  " B"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-required`

Within an interleaving, what must appear exactly once: \one.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | inline list | yes | What is required. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-required :content ("A"))
```

### Node kind `:bnf-indirection`

A non-terminal whose definition is spliced in place: \down.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The non-terminal. |

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-indirection :name "pattern")
```

### Node kind `:bnf-caret`

The caret character `^' of a syntax description: \hat.

Categories: `:inline`.

_No fields._

Example:

```lisp
(:bnf-caret)
```

### Node kind `:angle-name`

A name in angle brackets: \ang, the names of characters
(\NewlineChar) and \noargs.

Categories: `:inline`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The name, e.g. "Newline". |

Example:

```lisp
(:angle-name :name "Newline")
```

## Math

### Node kind `:math`

A formula: inline between $ and $, or displayed between $$ and $$.

Categories: `:inline`, `:block`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | boolean | no | True for a displayed formula. |
| `content` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The formula's list, in order. |
| `equation-number` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | A display's equation number, \eqno or \leqno; absent when it has none. |

### Node kind `:math-noad`

A noad: a nucleus of some class with its scripts.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | enumeration `math-class` | yes | The noad's class. |
| `limits` | boolean | no | True for an operator whose scripts go above and below (\limits). |
| `delimiter` | string | no | A radical's sign or an accent's character, as Unicode; absent for other classes. |
| `nucleus` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The nucleus: one character, or a subformula; absent for {}. |
| `superscript` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The superscript; absent when none. |
| `subscript` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The subscript; absent when none. |

### Node kind `:math-char`

A character of a formula, mapped from its family's font to Unicode.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The character, as Unicode. |

### Node kind `:math-fraction`

A fraction: \over, \atop, \above and their withdelims forms.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numerator` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The numerator. |
| `denominator` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | The denominator. |
| `no-rule` | boolean | no | True when no bar separates the two (\atop, or a zero thickness). |
| `left-delimiter` | string | no | The delimiter on the left of a withdelims form, as Unicode; absent otherwise. |
| `right-delimiter` | string | no | The delimiter on the right of a withdelims form, as Unicode; absent otherwise. |

### Node kind `:math-delimiter`

A delimiter that grows with its subformula: \left or \right.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `right` | boolean | no | True for \right, false for \left. |
| `text` | string | no | The delimiter, as Unicode; absent for the null delimiter (.). |

### Node kind `:math-style-change`

A change of style within a formula: \displaystyle, \textstyle,
\scriptstyle, \scriptscriptstyle.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | enumeration `math-style` | yes | The new style. |

### Node kind `:math-choice`

\mathchoice: four subformulas, of which TeX sets the one for the
style in force; all four are kept.

Categories: `:math-element`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | For display style. |
| `text` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | For text style. |
| `script` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | For script style. |
| `scriptscript` | list of node of kind or category `:math-element` | no | For scriptscript style. |

### Enumeration `math-class`

The class of a noad, as TeX gives it.

- `:ord` - An ordinary symbol.
- `:op` - A large operator (a sum, an integral).
- `:bin` - A binary operation.
- `:rel` - A relation.
- `:open` - An opening delimiter.
- `:close` - A closing delimiter.
- `:punct` - Punctuation.
- `:inner` - A delimited subformula (\left … \right).
- `:underline` - An underlined subformula (\underline).
- `:overline` - An overlined subformula (\overline).
- `:vcenter` - A box centred on the axis (\vcenter).
- `:radical` - A radical (\radical), its sign the noad's delimiter.
- `:accent` - An accented nucleus (\mathaccent), its accent the noad's.

### Enumeration `math-style`

A style of math, as TeX names it.

- `:display` - Display style (\displaystyle).
- `:text` - Text style (\textstyle).
- `:script` - Script style (\scriptstyle).
- `:scriptscript` - Scriptscript style (\scriptscriptstyle).

### Category `:math-element`

What a formula's list holds: noads, characters, fractions,
delimiters and style changes.

Kinds: `:math-noad`, `:math-char`, `:math-fraction`, `:math-delimiter`, `:math-style-change`, `:math-choice`.
